title: NYC bans AI use for students until they reach high school
slides: NYC bans student AI until high school—but why now?
This rule follows rising cheating incidents in middle schools.
Yet the ban excludes teachers, who can still use AI tools.
Middle schoolers must adapt to outdated methods until 9th grade.
Parents: ask schools how this prepares kids for AI-driven futures.
thread_text:
1. Wait, they banned AI? 

NYC just restricted student AI use until high school — no exceptions for middle schoolers. The stated reason? A rise in cheating incidents.

2. But teachers keep their tools.

The ban targets students only. Educators can still use AI for lesson plans and grading. So who exactly is being protected from what?

3. Outdated until freshman year.

Middle schoolers now practice handwriting and rote memorization while high schoolers get AI prep. That gap isn't neutral — it's a training divide.

4. What about the cheating hysteria?

The cheating spike is real, but the policy punishes everyone for a few. Instead of teaching responsible use, they removed the tool entirely.

5. Ask your school this today.

If you're a parent, ask: "How does delaying AI exposure until 9th grade prepare my child for an AI-driven workplace?" Demand a concrete answer.

instagram.caption:
Middle schoolers in NYC just lost access to AI tools until 9th grade—no exceptions, no pilot programs.  

The ban follows a spike in cheating incidents, but it only targets students. Teachers keep using AI for lesson plans and grading. So the message is: don't trust you with it, but we need it ourselves.  

Meanwhile, high schoolers get AI prep. That gap means two generations of students trained differently for the same job market.  

If your school adopts similar rules, ask: what concrete skill is my kid gaining by waiting?  

What would you tell a 13-year-old who asks why they're the only ones banned? 🤔📚🚫
